 Lance Bass shares the sweet holiday traditions he shares with his children 
 By 
 Vanessa Serna 
 Published 
 Nov. 17, 2026, 5:23 p.m. ET 
 See more of our coverage in your search results. 
 Make Page Six a Preferred Source 
 Lance Bass revealed his sweet holiday traditions with his kids, from driving to see Christmas lights to cozy movie nights.
 “Besides the normal decorating, our favorite thing to do is get in the car and go out to the rich neighborhoods and look at all the Christmas decorations,” the *NSYNC crooner told Page Six ahead of hosting the 25th Annual Christmas at The Grove Tree Lighting Celebration in Los Angeles on Monday.
 Bass gushed that he and his 5-year-old twins, Alexander James and Violet Betty, will “turn up the Christmas music as loud as it can go,” noting that one of the little ones’ favorite tracks is 1998’s “Merry Christmas, Happy Holidays” from the boy band’s “Home for Christmas” album. 
 12 
  Lance Bass opened up about sweet holiday traditions with his kids while chatting with Page Six at the 25th Anniversary Celebration of Christmas at the Grove in Los Angeles on Monday. Getty Images 
 12 
 The *NSYNC member shares twins Alexander James and Violet Betty with his husband Michael Turchin. (Seen above: The family of four.) Instagram/@lancebass

 “That’s the song they hear everywhere we go — the grocery store, an elevator, that’s what you’re going to hear,” Bass, who shares his kids with his husband, Michael Turchin, said. 
 “But I’m really trying to get them into more of the classics that we covered,” the “Bye, Bye, Bye” emcee, 47, added. 
 “My favorite was ‘O Holy Night’; that will always be my favorite. And especially my son, he loves harmonies, and so he really gets to geek out over that a cappella.” 
 12 
 Bass (seen here with his family) told us that he and his kids like to look at Christmas lights and watch one holiday movie per night. Instagram/@lancebass 
 12 
 Bass (seen above at The Grove on Monday) shared that one of his kids’ favorite track’s is *NSYNC’s 1998 “Merry Christmas, Happy Holidays” song from their “Home for Christmas” album. Variety via Getty Images 
 Aside from singing Christmas carols, Bass keeps the holiday spirit alive by trying to watch one themed movie a night with his family.
 When asked about his top three favorites, the “Gone” singer listed “A Christmas Story” (1983), “National Lampoon’s Christmas Vacation” (1989) and “Elf” (2003).
 As for Mark Ambor, 28, he told Page Six that his favorite tradition is “mistletoe,” though the “Belong Together” crooner didn’t divulge the details.
 12 
 Mark Ambor (seen here at The Grove Christmas event) told Page Six that his favorite Christmas tradition is mistletoe. Getty Images 
 12 
 You can catch the musician jamming out to “Run Rudolph Run” this season. Getty Images 
 The musician took the stage at the star-studded event to sing a rendition of Chuck Berry’s 1958 classic “Run Rudolph Run.” 
 Jason Mraz, 49, also stopped to chat with us on the carpet, sharing that holiday music is his favorite part of the Christmas season.
 “I’m the guy that sits at the house on the piano,” the Grammy-winning artist said, explaining he’s in charge of the playlist and will often play classics such as “The Christmas Song (Merry Christmas to You)” by the King Cole Trio (1946). 
 12 
 Jason Mraz told Page Six that his favorite Christmas tradition is playing holiday classics on the piano. Getty Images 
 12 
 The “I’m Yours” crooner performed “Snow in San Diego” at the event. Getty Images 
 Mraz also entertains his household with his own Christmas songs, including “Snow in San Diego,” which he performed later on in the night. The “I’m Yours” crooner plans to release an entire Christmas album in the next year. 
 Jamie Miller, 29, reflected on the success of the “past few months,” including his and Antonio Cipriano’s chart-topping song “Babydoll,” which recently won him the Kids’ Choice Award in the category of Favorite Viral Song.
 When Page Six asked the musician what he was thankful for, he responded, “Going number one in the UK. That’s the craziest thing that ever happened to me.” 
 12 
 As the year comes to an end, Jamie Miller reflected on the success of his and Antonio Cipriano’s chart-topping song “Babydoll.” Getty Images 
 12 
 The track reached No. 1 in the UK. (Seen here: Miller with Antonio Cipriano.) Getty Images

 Aside from jamming along to “Babydoll,” you’ll find Miller cranking up the speakers to Mariah Carey’s beloved Christmas anthem “All I Want for Christmas Is You” (1994).
 “Heated Rivalry” star Antonio Cipriano, 26, brought the energy and his brother Joseph Cipriano to the Christmas celebration, and couldn’t help but gush about how thankful he was for the latter.
 “I’m so grateful I get to do music right now,” the actor, who performed “Babydoll” with Miller, added.
 12 
 As for Antonio Cipriano (seen here performing at The Grove on Monday night), he had quite a list to be thankful for. Getty Images for Caruso 
 12 
 The actor performed “Santa Claus Is Coming to Town” at the event. Getty Images for Caruso 
 “This has been a dream of mine my entire life, and I’m really, really grateful for everything right now.”
 Antonio raved about his favorite tradition, eating his great-grandma’s famous artichoke pasta, and singing “Santa Claus Is Coming to Town,” the Frank Sinatra rendition, of course.
 The celebs came together to celebrate Christmas and light the 100-foot tree at the Rick Caruso-built outdoor mall before sending spectators home with a showstopping fireworks display.
